title: 2025 budget direction and Elora development approval
subtitle: Also: Hydro borrowing, operations centre contract, urban forestry fees, noise exemption fee deferral and AMO nomination.
overview: Council set draft direction for the 2025 budget {{vote:m9}}. Staff are to hold the tax rate increase to 4.5% or less before asset and termite management allocations, and raise fees and charges by 4.5% except where rates call for something different. No lower target was set. Staff will instead report on how the projected increase could be reduced, and councillors asked that fee increases be reviewed for their effect on residents and user groups.

Council approved Official Plan and zoning changes for a four-storey mixed-use building at 19-19A East Mill Street in Elora {{vote:m3}}. It awarded the Operations Centre design-build contract to Ball Construction Ltd. {{vote:m4}} and approved Centre Wellington Hydro's $4.7 million borrowing for station work in Elora and Fergus {{vote:m1}}.

Urban forestry fees were added to the fees by-law {{vote:m6}}. A proposed noise by-law exemption fee was sent back to staff for comparison with neighbouring municipalities {{vote:m5}}. Councillor Bronwynne Wilton, chosen by a draw of names, was nominated for the AMO Small Urban Caucus {{vote:m11}}. The Fergus Tennis Club agreement was pulled from the agenda so staff could hold more talks.

decisions.detail: Council gave staff direction for the 2025 draft budget, including a tax rate increase of 4.5% or less before asset and termite allocations, a 2% asset management increase, $88,500 for termite management and 4.5% fee increases {{vote:m9}}.
Council approved the Official Plan and zoning amendments, adopting Official Plan Amendment No. 15 for submission to the County, to allow a mixed-use development {{vote:m3}}.
Council awarded RFP #09-24 to Ball Construction Ltd. at a total upset limit of $1,446,330, excluding HST {{vote:m4}}.
As shareholder, Council approved the 2023 Shareholder Direction, annual report and audited statements, and secured $4.7 million in funding for distribution stations in Elora and Fergus {{vote:m1}}.
Council endorsed amendments to the 2024 Fees & Charges By-law to add fees related to urban forestry {{vote:m6}}.
Council referred the decision on this user fee to staff to compare fees in neighbouring municipalities {{vote:m5}}.
Council nominated Councillor Bronwynne Wilton for Director on the Small Urban Caucus of the AMO Board for 2024-2026 {{vote:m11}}.

debate: Hydro AGM questions covered the Milligan Park site for a new Fergus station, whether low-income assistance amounts should rise, retiree benefits and who maintains streetlights. Hydro said it works with a community group on assistance and would raise donations if the fund ran short.

On East Mill Street, public concerns about traffic, parking and height led the applicant to cut the building from five storeys to four and add parking. One councillor raised a resident's concern about restaurant hours. Staff said noise and geotechnical studies would be required at site plan stage.

On the Operations Centre, staff said eight bids were received. One councillor asked whether health care professionals could stay in the farmhouse during construction. Staff said that is not feasible and an alternate location will come to Council.

On the noise exemption fee, one councillor said it looked low compared with neighbouring municipalities and favoured a higher fee over increases for families. Another saw no point in deferring since no fee exists now. Staff said most requests are backyard weddings.

On the budget, councillors worried about residents facing another large increase and wanted the 4.5% lowered. They also asked that fee increases avoid recreation fees that affect families. Staff asked for a target to work toward. Council settled on a note asking for reduction options rather than a set number.
